extracted.intended_audience: investment company registrants, preparers, auditors, and SEC reporting professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on SEC Reg S-X Rule 6-11 reporting and related requirements for investment company registrants when acquiring (or proposing to acquire) funds, including significance tests, filing triggers, required financial statement periods, supplemental information, and special rules for private funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of 'significant subsidiary' definition on reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of significant subsidiary affects an investment company’s application of other SEC reporting rules (e.g., S-X Rule 3-09 for separate financial statements of significant subsidiaries not consolidated, and S-X Rule 4-08(g) for summarized financial information of subsidiaries not consolidated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-consolidated subsidiary (for example, a portfolio company) is significant under these rules, the registrant may be required to include separate financial statements or summarized financial information for that subsidiary. [SEC Rel 33-10786 sec II.E.1; S-X Rule 3-09; S-X Rule 4-08(g)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements used for significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance tests are performed by comparing: the most recent annual financial statements of each acquired fund (or combined for related funds) versus the registrant’s most recent annual financial statements filed at or prior to the date of acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, if the registrant has filed audited financial statements of a fund acquired after its latest fiscal year-end and provided required supplemental information, subsequent significance tests may use pro forma amounts that give effect to the previous acquisition. [S-X Rule 6-11(b)(3)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test (20% of total investments)
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquired fund is significant under the investment test if the total value of the registrant’s (and its subsidiaries’) investments in and advances to the acquired fund exceed 20% of the registrant’s consolidated total investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC uses total investments (not total assets) to focus the significance determination on impact to the investment portfolio and to provide transparency for registrants using a statement of net assets. The asset (total assets) test does not apply to investment company registrants. [S-X Rule 1-02(w)(2)(i); S-X Rule 6-11(b)(2)(ii)/(b)(3); SEC Rel 33-10786 sec II.E.1.a] Example calculations are provided to illustrate aggregation of investments and advances (including amounts from wholly owned subsidiaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test (change in net assets) and two-step requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquired fund is significant under the income test if (1) the absolute value of the change in net assets resulting from operations of the acquired fund exceeds 20% of the absolute value of the registrant’s consolidated change in net assets from operations, and (2) the investment test condition exceeds 5%. Both steps must be met for significance under the income test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrant’s most recent-year absolute change in net assets is at least 10% lower than the five-year average, the registrant may perform the income test using the five-year average absolute change in net assets. Detailed examples (including 5-year averaging) show calculation steps and thresholds. [S-X Rule 1-02(w)(2)(ii); S-X Rule 6-11(b)(2)(ii)/(b)(3); AICPA IC EP July 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision thresholds for filing financial statements (20% and 50% substitutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether financial statements and supplemental information must be filed depends on significance conditions, with substitution of 20% for specified 10% thresholds (and 50% substitution for aggregate impact tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the conditions set forth in §210.1-02(w)(2)(i) and (w)(2)(ii)(B), substituting 20% for 10% each place it appears, are satisfied, then financial statements and supplemental information are not required. If any such substituted-20% conditions are satisfied, financial statements (and supplemental info) must be filed. If aggregate post-balance-sheet acquisitions meet conditions substituting 50% for 10%, additional financial statements must be provided. [Reg S-X Rule 6-11(b)(2)(ii)/(iii) and paragraph (b)(2)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing triggers for fund acquisition under S-X Rule 6-11
rubrics_metrics.description: A filing requirement is triggered for an investment company registrant when (a) a fund acquisition has occurred during the most recent fiscal year or subsequent interim period for which a balance sheet is required, or (b) consummation of a fund acquisition has occurred or is probable after the date of the most recent filed balance sheet or after filing a post-effective amendment for a new series when no relevant balance sheet exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 6-11(a)(1) identifies these two situations; registrants must evaluate timing relative to their most recently filed audited balance sheet or post-effective filings. [S-X Rule 6-11(a)(1)(i)-(ii)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of filing for acquired (or to be acquired) fund
rubrics_metrics.description: When a filing requirement is triggered, the registrant must include the acquired fund’s financial statements (S-X Rule 3-01/3-02 or 3-18 as applicable), S-X Article 12 schedules, and the supplemental financial information specified in S-X Rule 6-11(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial statements and schedules must be prepared and audited in accordance with Reg S-X, including independence standards in S-X Rule 2-01 (or applicable independence standards if fund is not a registrant). For registered management investment companies, Rule 3-18 applies; for other registrants, Rule 3-01/3-02 apply. [S-X Rule 6-11(a)(1); S-X Rules 3-01/3-02/3-18; S-X Rule 2-01; S-X Article 12]

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods to present for acquired fund financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquired fund is subject to Rule 3-18, present the periods described in Rule 3-18 (generally two years for statement of changes in net assets and one year for other statements). If not subject to Rule 3-18, present the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the above periods must be filed depends on the registration scenario and significance thresholds (see decision tree). Fiscal-year statements must be audited except as noted for certain proxy filings or Form N-14 exceptions. [S-X Rule 6-11(b)(2)(ii)-(iii); S-X Rule 3-18]

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time filing of acquired fund financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate financial statements and supplemental information of an acquired fund need only be filed once and are not required to be included in subsequent filings or shareholder reports of the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 6-11(b)(4) — the one-time filing requirement reduces repetitive inclusion in later filings/reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquired fund’s prior SEC filings do not eliminate registrant’s requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an acquired fund previously filed financial statements with the SEC, the investment company registrant’s obligation to file acquired-fund financial statements under S-X Rule 6-11 is not eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC views the requirement as primarily for the registrant’s shareholders. Some forms (e.g., Form N-14) permit backward incorporation by reference; registrants should consult form instructions (General Instruction G to Form N-14). [SEC Rel 33-10786 sec II.E.2.c (n 405)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisitions involving private funds — permitted compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquired fund would be an investment company but for sections 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7) exclusions (i.e., private funds), the required financial statements may comply with US GAAP and only S-X Article 12 (instead of full Reg S-X). For private accounts managed by an investment adviser, provide Article 12 schedules for assets acquired or to be acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 6-11(c) permits this limited compliance to balance investor information needs and cost. Registrants must still provide schedules specified in Article 12. [S-X Rule 6-11(c)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Audited financial statements required for acquired private funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when an acquired fund is private, S-X Rule 6-11 requires audited financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC's view is that audited statements ensure investors receive appropriate information; many private funds already prepare audited statements for other regulatory or contractual reasons. Registrants should obtain audited statements for acquired private funds. [SEC Rel 33-10786 sec II.E.2.c; S-X Rule 6-11(a)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Private fund financial statements compliance requirements (no full Reg S-X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of an acquired (or to be acquired) private fund need not comply with Reg S-X in full but must be audited, comply with US GAAP, and comply with S-X Article 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach balances cost (avoiding full Reg S-X reissuance) while requiring adequate investor disclosure (Article 12 schedules listing each investment). Registrants and auditors will likely have to perform incremental work to meet Article 12 detail. [S-X Rule 6-11(c); S-X Rule 6-11(a)/(d)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of condensed SOI under US GAAP vs S-X Article 12
rubrics_metrics.description: A condensed schedule of investments (SOI) prepared under US GAAP is typically not sufficient to satisfy S-X Article 12 because Article 12 requires more prescriptive and granular detail (e.g., listing investments separately rather than aggregating items under 5% thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies that use US GAAP condensed SOI should expect to perform incremental disclosure and auditing procedures to produce an S-X Article 12-compliant SOI. [S-X Rules 12-12 – 12-29; US GAAP reference 946-210-50-6]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of combined financial statements for acquired private funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined financial statements may be appropriate for commonly controlled entities when more meaningful than separate statements, but S-X Rule 6-11 does not explicitly allow combined presentations; they may be used for SEC reporting if Subtopic 810-10 requirements are met and the combined presentation is consistent with S-X Rule 6-11 objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff has indicated combined statements could satisfy S-X Rule 6-11 in certain situations but registrants should consider whether all funds presented on a combined basis are included in the acquisition; if only a portion is acquired, combined presentation may not provide sufficient information about assets acquired. Registrants are encouraged to seek staff guidance when considering combined presentations. [810-10-55-1B; S-X Rule 6-11 commentary]

rubrics_metrics.name: Required supplemental financial information in lieu of pro forma
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11 requires supplemental financial information instead of pro forma financial statements for fund acquisitions; the supplemental information must include a fee table (current and pro forma fees, if different), an SOI modified for material portfolio changes due to investment restrictions (with narrative), and narrative disclosure of material differences in accounting policies between the acquired fund and the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information is provided in lieu of pro forma §§210.11-01 through 210.11-03 and focuses on: (i) fees, (ii) expected material changes in the acquired fund’s investment portfolio, and (iii) material accounting policy differences. The staff has also provided views on pro forma fee and capitalization tables for complex merger scenarios involving multiple potential outcomes. [S-X Rule 6-11(d); IM-DCFO 1995-11]

rubrics_metrics.name: Format guidance for the fee table
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11 does not prescribe a specific format for the fee table; instead, registrants should use the format prescribed in the appropriate registration statement under the Investment Company Act (e.g., Form N-1A for open-end funds, Form N-2 for closed-end funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relevant item and instructions on Form N-1A (Item 3 Risk/Return Summary: Fee Table) or Form N-2 (Item 3 Fee Table and Synopsis) when preparing the fee table required as part of S-X Rule 6-11 supplemental information. [S-X Rule 6-11(d)(1)(i)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for requiring supplemental information rather than pro forma statements
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11 replaced prior pro forma requirements to better align acquired-fund reporting with investors’ information needs and to reduce costs and potential investor confusion arising from applying acquisition rules not designed for investment companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information focuses on material items most relevant to shareholders (fees, portfolio changes, accounting policy differences) and reduces burden that historically outweighed investor benefit under prior pro forma requirements. Examples and staff views may guide presentation for complex transactions. [S-X Rule 6-11(d); background discussion]
